result.title: Analyzing Code Provenance in LLMs for Programming Education
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) play an increasing role in programming education, challenging traditional assessment methods as they can generate fully functional code instantly. This disrupts the reliability of student submissions as indicators of learning and effort. To address this issue, code provenance is essential for tracing the origins of code and distinguishing student-authored, AI-generated, and externally sourced components. We extend the Min-K% probability approach by incorporating synthetic non-member code generation and apply it to Python code for membership inference and provenance tracking. Evaluations cover free LLMs such as GPT-2, DistilGPT-2, and DialoGPT, as well as state-of-the-art commercial models including GPT-5, Gemini 2.5, Mistral, DeepSeek, and LLaMA 3.3. Before evaluating our approach on higher-education student assignments, we validate its feasibility using Stack Overflow data. The results show that free models enable more sensitive code memorization detection than commercial models. By systematically comparing these LLMs, we assess trade-offs between detection accuracy and privacy protection, taking an initial step toward effective assessment of AI-assisted programming education through combined provenance detection and process visibility.

AI.brief_summary: 论文面向编程教育中的代码来源追踪问题，扩展 Min-K% 概率方法并结合合成非成员代码生成，对多种开源与商用 LLM 进行成员推断与 AI 生成代码识别，并在 Stack Overflow 与高校作业数据上验证可行性。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究目标是代码来源判别与教育评估，其基于 token 概率的成员检测既未涉及视觉或多模态内部状态，也未处理证据筛选、动态计算与停止决策，与 LVR 主线的状态表示和推理机制没有实质联系。
